title: Tone Primer
desc: Hear the six tones, read Jyutping, and hear tones in words you already know

words.note: Tone 1 · high and flat, like holding a high note.
Tone 2 · starts mid and rises high, like a surprised 'eh?'.
Tone 3 · mid and flat, your normal speaking pitch.
Tone 4 · low and falling, the bottom of your voice.
Tone 5 · starts low and rises only to mid — a smaller rise than tone 2.
Tone 6 · low and flat, just under tone 3.
Tone 1 + tone 1: both syllables high and level. Keep the pitch up for the whole word.
Tone 2 rises from mid to high, then tone 1 stays high and level.
Tone 2: rises from mid to high, like a surprised "eh?". oe ≈ French "eu".
Tone 1 then tone 3: high, then your normal mid pitch.
Tone 4 then tone 1: start at the bottom of your voice, jump to the top.
Tone 6 + tone 6: low and level, just under your normal pitch.
Tone 4: low and falling. Compare 點 (dim2), which rises.
Tone 4, long aa. Compare 行 (haang4) "to walk": same tone, but it ends in -ng.

grammar.title: Six tones, one chart
grammar.explain: Pitch is part of the word. Imagine your voice range as 5 steps: tone 1 sits at the top (5), tone 3 in the middle (3), tone 6 just below (2), tone 4 drops to the bottom (1). Tone 2 rises from the middle to the top (3→5); tone 5 rises only a little, from low to mid (2→3). Every Jyutping syllable ends with its tone number.

examples.en: poem, history, try, time, market, matter

grammar.title: Reading Jyutping
grammar.explain: j = English y · z ≈ ts without a puff of air (close to 'dz') · c ≈ ts with a puff of air · yu = French u · eo / oe ≈ French eu · aa is long, a is short · final -p, -t, -k are not released: the syllable is just cut short.
